This module quotes 45 CFR 164.314(a) and 164.504(e)(1)-(2) in full, verbatim, from
`sources/cfr/45-164-business-associate-excerpt.md` — the only source used. 164.308(b), 164.410, and
164.502(e) are named only, because they're referenced repeatedly by the saved excerpt but weren't
independently fetched this session; don't look to this module for their specific mechanics.

**A note on eCFR's own site, read before the links below:** this session tried, directly, to load
eCFR's own human-readable pages for both sections — the same `www.ecfr.gov/current/...` URLs
recorded in the saved source file. Every attempt (plain `curl`, with a browser user-agent, with
compression) redirected to `unblock.federalregister.gov`, a bot-protection wall blocking this
environment specifically — the same class of block `reading-an-iso-27001-certificate` hit on
`iso.org`. The eCFR Versioner API itself (the machine-readable data source, reached with
`--compressed`) *did* return the current section text successfully (HTTP 200), confirming eCFR's
underlying data is live and matches what's quoted above — but that API endpoint isn't a page meant
for a person to open and read. In its place, the links below go to GovInfo (the U.S. Government
Publishing Office's own official archive, the same underlying government source eCFR itself
republishes), each directly curl-verified this session:

- **[164.314 — GovInfo, CFR title 45, volume 2](https://www.govinfo.gov/app/details/CFR-2023-title45-vol2/CFR-2023-title45-vol2-sec164-314)**
  — the official U.S. Government Publishing Office page for this section. Curl-verified this
  session: HTTP 200 from `govinfo.gov`. Like several client-rendered government sites this
  curriculum has already encountered (AICPA in `reading-a-soc-2-report`), the page's title tag
  doesn't carry section-specific text to grep for — verified by status code and domain, plus a
  direct check of GovInfo's underlying XML for this section (also HTTP 200), which was read and
  confirmed to match the text quoted in this lesson word for word.
- **[164.504 — GovInfo, CFR title 45, volume 2](https://www.govinfo.gov/app/details/CFR-2023-title45-vol2/CFR-2023-title45-vol2-sec164-504)**
  — the same official archive's page for 164.504. Curl-verified HTTP 200 the same way, including a
  direct check of the underlying XML against the text quoted above.
- **If you're checking these yourself later:** try eCFR's own current-text pages first —
  `https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C/part-164/subpart-C/section-164.314`
  and `.../subpart-E/section-164.504` — since this session's block is specific to this environment
  and may not affect a normal browser. GovInfo's annual-edition text (above) is official and
  verified current against this excerpt, but eCFR's own "current" page reflects amendments in real
  time, which is the better source going forward if it loads for you.

**Internal links:**

- **[Reading a SOC 2 Report](../reading-a-soc-2-report/index.qmd)** — module 2. This module's
  safeguards-clause discussion ((e)(2)(ii)(B)) points back to this vendor's Type II report and its
  Security/Availability Trust Services Criteria as the kind of evidence a vendor would offer to show
  it's actually meeting a BAA's safeguards requirement.
- **[Reading an ISO 27001 Certificate](../reading-an-iso-27001-certificate/index.qmd)** — module 3.
  Its change-management and supplier-relationships Statement of Applicability findings are the other
  half of that same safeguards-and-subcontractor-flow-down evidence picture.

  (HIPAA Vault, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson. A commercial
  HIPAA-compliance vendor's general BAA explainer; industry training content, not regulator
  guidance, and not specific to Lakeshore. Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11
  (HTTP 200). No HHS OCR video squarely on BAAs was found: OCR's own channel has a "Risk
  Management Under the HIPAA Security Rule" video, but it is about risk management, not
  business associate contracts, so it was not embedded.
- **[Cornell LII: 45 CFR 164.504, current text](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.504)**
  — a readable mirror of the Privacy Rule section quoted in this lesson, useful for checking
  current text against the dated snapshot. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[Cornell LII: 45 CFR 164.314, current text](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.314)**
  — the Security Rule side of the same contract checklist. Verified loading via `curl` on

- **[Cornell LII: 45 CFR 164.502](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.502)** — the section
  (paragraph (e)) that 164.504(e)(1) cross-references for when a BAA is required at all. This

- **[Cornell LII: 45 CFR 164.308](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.308)** — contains
  paragraph (b), which 164.314(a)(1) cross-references for the Security Rule's business associate

  (HTTP 200).
- **[Cornell LII: 45 CFR 164.410](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.410)** — the

- **[Cornell LII: 45 CFR 160.103, definitions](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/160.103)**
  — where "business associate" itself is defined, including who counts as a subcontractor. Read

- **[Federal Register: Omnibus Rule, January 25, 2013](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2013/01/25/2013-01073/modifications-to-the-hipaa-privacy-security-enforcement-and-breach-notification-rules-under-the)**
  — the final rule that extended HIPAA obligations to business associates and their

  the preamble sections on business associates. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11

## Keep learning

Not official sources — good places to learn more about business associate agreements and healthcare vendor risk.

- **[HIPAA Business Associate Agreement](https://www.hipaajournal.com/hipaa-business-associate-agreement/)** (HIPAA Journal) — a long-running independent HIPAA news and guidance site explaining what a BAA is, who needs one and common mistakes; a plain-English companion to the lesson. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[The Complicated Nature of BA Compliance](https://www.hipaajournal.com/baa-compliance/)** (HIPAA Journal) — why BAA compliance is harder than signing a form, including when the business associate isn't the only party at fault. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[Vendor Management Guidance](https://www.in.gov/cybersecurity/government/best-practices-standards-and-resources/healthcare-vendor-management-guidance-helps-ensure-patient-safety-information-security/vendor-management-guidance)** (Indiana Cybersecurity Hub, state government) — a healthcare-focused vendor management guide, useful for HCISPP-style thinking about contracts, subcontractors and oversight. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[The Complete Guide to Healthcare Third-Party Risk Management](https://www.censinet.com/perspectives/the-complete-guide-to-healthcare-third-party-risk-management-from-basics-to-advanced-strategies)** (Censinet — vendor/commercial content) — a broad healthcare TPRM overview that places the BAA inside a full vendor lifecycle; supports HCISPP third-party risk study. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
